Ang kolasisi! Natutulog itong nakabaligtad, nakabitin sa sanga gaya ng paniki.
copy.bis:
Unsang langgam ang matulog nga baliktad?

Ang kolasisi! Matulog kini nga nakabaligtad, nagbitay sa sanga sama sa kabog.

Kapag barado ang ilong mo, hindi makaabot sa smell cells ang amoy ng pagkain — at dahil magkasama ang amoy at lasa, nawawala ang linamnam!

Sayop nga pagtuo nga matabangan usab ang host sa commensalism. Sa tinuod, usa ra ang makabenepisyo — walay makuha ang host, basta dili usab madaot.

copy.en: Evolution shows that similar species came from a shared ancestor long ago — the more DNA and body traits two animals share, the more closely related they are.
copy.tl: Ipinapakita ng evolution na nagmula sa iisang ninuno noong una ang magkakatulad na species — kung gaano kalapit ang DNA at katawan ng dalawang hayop, siyang nagpapakita kung gaano sila kalapit na magkamag-anak.
copy.bis: Gipakita sa evolution nga ang managsama nga mga species naggikan sa usa ka komon nga katigulangan kaniadto — kung unsa kadaghan ang panag-ingnan sa DNA ug lawas sa duha ka hayop, mao kana ang nagpakita kung unsa sila ka suod nga paryente.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a scientific name gives everyone one clear, shared name
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why scientific names are used (to avoid confusion from varying common names). It does not teach classification into groups using a table, nor does it mention the named groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, mammals, reptiles, etc.). Scientific nomenclature is related to taxonomy but does not directly support this classification competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a scientific name gives everyone one clear, shared name
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the importance of the six-kingdom system and the three-domain system of classification of living things
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the purpose of scientific names, not the six-kingdom or three-domain classification systems. It provides no information about kingdoms, domains, or their importance, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
Why do scientists use scientific names?

A common name for an animal or plant changes from place to place and language to language, which is confusing — a scientific name gives everyone one clear, shared name.
copy.tl:
Bakit gumagamit ng siyentipikong pangalan?

Nagbabago ang karaniwang pangalan ng hayop o halaman sa bawat lugar at wika, kaya nakakalito — ang pangalang siyentipiko ang nagbibigay ng iisang malinaw na pangalan para sa lahat.
copy.bis:
Ngano gigamit ang siyentipikong ngalan?

Nagbag-o ang ordinaryong ngalan sa mananap o tanom sa matag dapit ug pinulongan, mao nga makalibog — ang ngalang siyentipiko naghatag og usa ka klaro nga ngalan alang sa tanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The very first magnetic compass was developed a very long time ago in ancient China!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a science invention (the magnetic compass) but does not use information from the home or local community, nor does it explain the invention's impact on everyday life. It only states the historical origin, so it does not directly support the competency's required actions.

copy.en: The very first magnetic compass was developed a very long time ago in ancient China!
copy.tl: Ang unang magnetic compass (kompas) ay binuo noong sinaunang panahon sa bansang Tsina, grabe di ba!
copy.bis: Ang unang magnetic compass (kompas) gimugna kaniadto sa karaang China, grabe ka nindot niini, 'di ba!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mixing complementary lights, like red and cyan, combines to make white light.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses color mixing and complementary colors on a color wheel, which touches on light behavior but does not address sources of light, how light can be changed in the sense intended by the competency, or uses in everyday situations. The content is more about color theory than the Grade 3 light sources/behavior/uses competency.

copy.en:
What are complementary colours?

They sit opposite on the colour wheel, like red and green! Mixing complementary lights, like red and cyan, combines to make white light.
copy.tl:
Ano ang complementary colours?

Nasa magkasalungat sila sa colour wheel, tulad ng red at green! Kapag pinagsama ang complementary lights tulad ng red at cyan, nagiging white light!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang complementary colours?

Nag-atbang sila sa colour wheel, sama sa red ug green! Kung i-mix ang complementary lights sama sa red ug cyan, mahimong white light!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Beetles go through complete metamorphosis too—a plump grub living in soil or wood grows, becomes a pupa, then emerges as a beetle with hard wing covers.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes beetle life-cycle stages but does not use a flow chart or compare stages across animals as required by the competency. It only provides a textual example of one animal's metamorphosis, which is related content but not direct instructional support for the specified skill.

copy.en: Beetles go through complete metamorphosis too—a plump grub living in soil or wood grows, becomes a pupa, then emerges as a beetle with hard wing covers.
copy.tl: Dumadaan din ang mga salagubang sa kumpletong metamorphosis—ang kanilang uod na kumakain sa lupa o kahoy ay lumalaki, nagiging pupa, at lumalabas bilang salagubang na may matigas na pakpak.
copy.bis: Moagi usab ang mga bakukang sa kompleto nga metamorphosis—ang ilang ulod nga nagpuyo sa yuta o kahoy motubo, mahimong pupa, ug mogula isip bakukang nga adunay gahi nga tabon sa pako.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Complete metamorphosis doesn't take the same time for every insect
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses variation in the duration of complete metamorphosis in insects, but does not use a flow chart, does not compare the stages of a life cycle, and does not address the named animals (butterfly, frog, chicken, human). It only shares a general fact about metamorphosis timing, which is related to life cycles but does not directly support the competency's required activity.

copy.en: Complete metamorphosis doesn't take the same time for every insect — some finish in days or weeks, others take months, especially when it's cooler.
copy.tl: Hindi pare-pareho ang tagal ng kumpletong metamorphosis — may natatapos sa ilang araw o linggo, may umaabot naman ng buwan, lalo na kapag malamig.
copy.bis: Dili managsama ang gidugayon sa kompleto nga metamorphosis — adunay mahuman sulod sa pipila ka adlaw o semana, ang uban moabot og bulan, ilabina kon bugnaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: No! The tutubi has no pupa stage — just egg, then nymph in water, then dragonfly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the dragonfly life cycle (egg, nymph, adult) and notes it is incomplete metamorphosis, but it does not use a flow chart to compare stages, which is the format-required activity for G4-L-5. The content is about a life cycle but not the specific skill of comparing stages via flow charts, and the animal is not among the listed examples.

copy.en:
Does the dragonfly go through complete metamorphosis?

No! The tutubi has no pupa stage — just egg, then nymph in water, then dragonfly. That makes it incomplete metamorphosis.
copy.tl:
Kumpleto ba ang metamorphosis ng tutubi?

Hindi! Walang pupa ang tutubi — itlog lang, tapos nymph sa tubig, tapos tutubi na. Kaya di-kumpletong metamorphosis ang tawag dito.
copy.bis:
Kompleto ba ang metamorphosis sa alindahaw?

Dili! Walay pupa ang alindahaw — itlog lang, dayon nymph sa tubig, dayon alindahaw na. Mao nga dili kompleto nga metamorphosis ang tawag niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has several vents or cones! Taal Volcano is a great example of this.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a complex volcano as having multiple vents or cones, which is a structural feature. The competency G8-E-3 requires describing volcano types according to activity, eruption type, and location in the crust. The card does not address any of these three criteria, so it only shares the broad topic of volcanoes without directly supporting the competency.

copy.en:
What makes a complex volcano special?

It has several vents or cones! Taal Volcano is a great example of this.
copy.tl:
Ano ang espesyal sa isang complex volcano?

May maraming bunganga o kono ito! Ang Bulkang Taal ay isang magandang halimbawa.
copy.bis:
Unsay espesyal sa usa ka complex volcano?

Adunay daghang buho o kono kini! Ang Bulkang Taal maayo nga panig-ingnan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Healthy compost needs a mix of two things: wet green scraps and dry brown leaves.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that compost needs a mix of green and brown materials. It does not describe any chemical property such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. Composting is tangentially related to biodegradability, but the card provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Healthy compost needs a mix of two things: wet green scraps and dry brown leaves.
copy.tl: Ang masustansyang compost ay nangangailangan ng halo ng basang berdeng tira ng pagkain at tuyong kayumangging dahon.
copy.bis: Ang himsog nga compost nagkinahanglan og sagol nga basa nga lunhaw nga sagbot ug uga nga brown nga dahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Turn or mix the pile! This lets in more air so it breaks down quicker
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Turning a compost pile for air is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This lets in more air so it breaks down quicker
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: Adding air to a pile is not describing chemical properties such as burnt, reactive, or biodegradable.

copy.en: Want faster compost? Turn or mix the pile! This lets in more air so it breaks down quicker.
copy.tl: Gusto mo bang mas mabilis matunaw ang compost? Ihalo o baliktarin ito! Mas maraming hangin ang papasok kaya mas mabilis itong mabubulok.
copy.bis: Gusto ba nimo nga paspas madunot ang compost? Ukaya o baliktara kini! Mas daghang hangin ang mosulod busa mas paspas kini madunot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a liquid also drains from a worm bin that can be made into 'worm tea'
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions liquid and solid castings but does not teach the three states of matter or their properties. It is about fertilizer, not states of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: used by gardeners as a liquid fertilizer poured or sprayed on plants
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card concerns applying fertilizer to plants but does not discuss outer plant parts (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in taking up water and nutrients. Only the general topic of plants connects it.

copy.en: Besides solid castings, a liquid also drains from a worm bin that can be made into 'worm tea' — diluted with water and used by gardeners as a liquid fertilizer poured or sprayed on plants.
copy.tl: Bukod sa solidong casting, may likido ring tumutulo sa worm bin na magiging 'worm tea' — hinahaluan ito ng tubig at ginagamit ng mga magtatanim bilang likidong pataba na ibinubuhos o isinisprey sa halaman.
copy.bis: Gawas sa solido nga casting, adunay usab likido nga motulo sa worm bin nga mahimong 'worm tea' — sagolan kini og tubig ug gamiton sa mga hardinero isip likido nga abono nga ibubo o i-spray sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A compound is a pure substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a compound as a pure substance with a fixed ratio of elements. It does not describe chemical properties of materials such as burning, reacting, or being degradable/biodegradable, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A compound is a pure substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio.
copy.tl: Ang compound ay isang pure substance na gawa sa dalawa o higit pang element na chemically combined sa fixed ratio.
copy.bis: Ang compound usa ka pure substance nga gihimo sa duha o daghan pang element nga chemically combined sa fixed ratio.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A computer is an electronic machine that follows instructions called programs to store, organize, and process information very quickly!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a computer, which is a science invention, but it does not instruct students to use information from home or the local community, nor does it explain the computer's impact on everyday life. It only provides a basic definition, so it does not directly support the competency's skill of identifying an invention from local sources and explaining its impact.

copy.en: A computer is an electronic machine that follows instructions called programs to store, organize, and process information very quickly!
copy.tl: Ang kompyuter ay isang makinang elektroniko na sumusunod sa mga utos na tinatawag na programa upang mag-imbak, mag-ayos, at magproseso ng impormasyon nang napakabilis!
copy.bis: Ang kompyuter usa ka elektronikong makina nga mosunod sa mga mando nga gitawag og programa aron magtipig, mag-ayos, ug magproseso og impormasyon nga paspas kaayo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Add a little water to calamansi juice—it stays super sour! Add lots of water, and it turns mild.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: express quantitatively the amount of solute present in a given volume of solvent
assignedReviews.reason: The card qualitatively describes how dilution (adding water) changes sourness, which relates to concentration, but it does not express quantitatively the amount of solute in a given volume of solvent. No measurements, units, or numerical expressions are provided, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Add a little water to calamansi juice—it stays super sour! Add lots of water, and it turns mild. That's concentration controlling the taste!
copy.tl: Kung kaunting tubig lang ang idadagdag sa calamansi juice, sobrang maasim pa rin! Pero kung maraming tubig, magiging malambot ang lasa. Iyan ang konsentrasyon!
copy.bis: Kon gamay ra ang tubig nga idugang sa kalamansi juice, maasim pa gihapon! Pero kon daghan ang tubig, mahumok ang lasa. Mao na ang konsentrasyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It hardens because of a chemical reaction with water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies concrete hardening as a chemical reaction but does not explain why physical changes are reversible and chemical changes are irreversible, which is the core action of G6-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It hardens because of a chemical reaction with water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a chemical reaction but does not explain the formation of new bonds or breaking of existing bonds, nor the formation of a new substance, which is the specific focus of G9-M-2.

copy.en:
Does concrete harden just by drying out in the sun?

Nope! It hardens because of a chemical reaction with water, not just because it dries out.
copy.tl:
Natutuyo lang ba sa araw para tumigas ang konkreto?

Hindi! Tumitigas ito dahil sa isang reaksyong kemikal sa tubig, hindi dahil natutuyo lang ito.
copy.bis:
Nauga lang ba sa adlaw aron mogahi ang konkreto?

Dili! Mogahi kini tungod sa reaksyong kemikal sa tubig, dili tungod kay nauga lang kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Concrete is first poured as a wet mix into a mold, where it hardens perfectly into that shape!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card illustrates that a wet mix takes the shape of a mold and then hardens into a solid with that shape, touching on liquid and solid shape behavior. However, it does not describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume as a set, and it does not address volume or gases. It is a single everyday example rather than direct instruction on the competency.

copy.en: Concrete is first poured as a wet mix into a mold, where it hardens perfectly into that shape!
copy.tl: Ibinubuhos muna ang konkreto bilang wet mix sa isang mold, at doon ito tumitigas ayon sa hugis nito!
copy.bis: Ang konkreto ibubo una isip wet mix ngadto sa mold, ug didto kini mogahi sumala sa porma niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An object moves at constant speed when it covers equal distances in each second!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines constant speed, which is a prerequisite concept for graphing uniform speed, but it does not involve constructing or labeling graphs, nor does it address stationary or fast/slow speeds as required by the competency.

copy.en:
What does constant speed mean?

An object moves at constant speed when it covers equal distances in each second!
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng constant speed?

Ang isang bagay ay may pare-parehong bilis kapag pantay ang layong nararating nito sa bawat segundo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pasabot sa constant speed?

Ang usa ka butang adunay pirme nga katulin kung pareho ang gilay-on nga maabot niini matag segundo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Orion sits high and bright in the night sky. In hot summer, you can barely see it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card notes that Orion is visible in certain months and barely visible in summer, which touches on 'changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year.' However, the competency requires making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects, including seasons and star patterns. The card provides no model, no explanation of the cause, and no connection to the Sun-Earth-Moon system. It only states an observation, so it does not directly support the competency's required activity or explanation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: During the cool months from December to February, when the amihan wind blows! Orion sits high and bright in the night sky.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card links Orion's visibility to the cool months (amihan season), which is a seasonal association. However, the competency asks students to explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons. The card does not mention ancient cultures, direction-finding, or how constellations were used to verify seasons. It only states a modern observation of Orion's seasonal visibility, so it does not directly support the competency's historical/cultural explanation.

copy.en:
When is the best time to spot Orion in the Philippines?

During the cool months from December to February, when the amihan wind blows! Orion sits high and bright in the night sky. In hot summer, you can barely see it.
copy.tl:
Kailan pinakamagandang makita ang Orion sa Pilipinas?

Tuwing malamig na buwan mula Disyembre hanggang Pebrero, kapag umiihip ang amihan! Mataas at maliwanag ito sa langit sa gabi. Tuwing tag-init, halos hindi mo ito makikita.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a pinakamaayong makita ang Orion sa Pilipinas?

Panahon sa bugnaw nga mga bulan gikan Disyembre hangtod Pebrero, kon ang amihan mohuyop! Taas ug hayag kini sa langit sa gabii. Panahon sa init nga ting-init, halos dili nimo kini makita.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cooking oil is thicker, or more viscous, than water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires describing properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. The card discusses viscosity and flow rate, which are different liquid properties and do not directly support the shape/volume distinction.

copy.en: Cooking oil is thicker, or more viscous, than water. Because of this, it flows much more slowly when you pour it from a bottle!
copy.tl: Mas malapot, o mas viscous, ang mantika kaysa tubig. Kaya naman, mas mabagal itong dumadaloy kapag ibinubuhos mo ito mula sa bote!
copy.bis: Mas labot, o mas viscous, ang mantika kay sa tubig. Busa, mas hinay kini modagayday kon ibubo nimo kini gikan sa botelya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Nicolaus Copernicus was a Polish astronomer from Poland!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Copernicus as a famous foreign scientist but does not mention any invention or contribution, which is a required part of the competency. It only provides his nationality and profession, so it does not directly support identifying a scientist and their invention.

copy.en: Nicolaus Copernicus was a Polish astronomer from Poland! He was a very smart astronomer.
copy.tl: Si Nicolaus Copernicus ay isang astronomong Polako mula sa Poland! Siya ay matalinong astronomo.
copy.bis: Si Nicolaus Copernicus usa ka astronomong Polako gikan sa Poland! Siya maalamon nga astronomo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Coral islands are usually low and flat! They are made of sandy bits and crushed limestone from old coral and shells.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a landform (coral island) but does not describe how it influences non-living and living components of the environment, nor does it provide local examples as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Coral islands are usually low and flat! They are made of sandy bits and crushed limestone from old coral and shells.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sandy bits and crushed limestone, which are rock-related materials, but it does not involve exploring, observing, or collecting rocks, nor comparing features like texture, color, or grain crystal size as the competency requires.

copy.en: Coral islands are usually low and flat! They are made of sandy bits and crushed limestone from old coral and shells.
copy.tl: Ang mga coral island ay karaniwang mababa at patag! Gawa sila sa buhangin at durog na apog mula sa mga coral at kabibe.
copy.bis: Ang mga coral island kasagaran ubos ug patag! Gama kini sa balas ug dugmok nga apog gikan sa mga coral ug kabhang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hard coral polyps build a stony skeleton that forms the reef, while soft coral polyps have no hard skeleton and sway like a plant
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: Stony versus soft skeletons are not head, legs or wings used to move and gather food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hard coral polyps build a stony skeleton that forms the reef, while soft coral polyps have no hard skeleton
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Coral skeleton types are not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en: Hard coral polyps build a stony skeleton that forms the reef, while soft coral polyps have no hard skeleton and sway like a plant.
copy.tl: Ang mga polyp ng hard coral ay gumagawa ng matigas na kalansay na bumubuo ng bahura, habang ang soft coral ay walang matigas na kalansay kaya umuugoy parang halaman.
copy.bis: Ang mga polyp sa hard coral naghimo og gahi nga kalansay nga mao ang nagtukod sa bahura, samtang ang soft coral walay gahi nga kalansay busa nagtabyog sama sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Coriolis effect happens because Earth spins on its axis, making moving air and water appear to curve.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the Coriolis effect as a consequence of Earth's rotation, but the competency requires demonstrating rotation using a globe to explain day and night. The card does not address day/night or the globe demonstration, so it only shares the broad topic of Earth's rotation without directly supporting the stated skill.

copy.en: The Coriolis effect happens because Earth spins on its axis, making moving air and water appear to curve.
copy.tl: Nangyayari ang Coriolis effect dahil umiikot ang Earth sa axis niya, kaya parang lumiliko ang hangin at tubig.
copy.bis: Mahitabo ang Coriolis effect tungod kay nagtuyok ang Earth sa iyang axis, mao nga morag mokurba ang hangin ug tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cork floats in water because its density is lower than water's!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about factors affecting the movement of objects (size, shape, heaviness, material, surface texture). The card explains floating via density, which is not one of the listed factors and does not address movement of objects. It shares the topic of objects in water but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cork floats in water because its density is lower than water's!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The competency defines matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. The card discusses density and buoyancy, which are properties of matter but do not directly teach the definition of matter as having mass and volume. It is related background but not direct support.

copy.en: Cork floats in water because its density is lower than water's!
copy.tl: Lumulutang ang cork sa tubig dahil mas mababa ang densidad nito kaysa sa tubig!
copy.bis: Molutaw ang cork sa tubig kay mas ubos ang density niini kaysa sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As corn ripens, its once soft, pale silk slowly turns brown and dry.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: Ripening color change is a living-thing change, not a description of grow, respond, and reproduce as characteristics of living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As corn ripens, its once soft, pale silk slowly turns brown and dry.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: One ripening cue is not a comparison of mammal, bird, and plant life cycles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its once soft, pale silk slowly turns brown and dry
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Silk color as a ripeness sign does not describe pollination, seed production, or propagation.

copy.en: As corn ripens, its once soft, pale silk slowly turns brown and dry.
copy.tl: Habang naghihinog ang mais, unti-unting nagiging kayumanggi at tuyo ang dating malambot at maputlang silk nito.

Ang agos ng kuryente ay sinusukat sa amperes (A)! Ipinangalan ito kay Andre-Marie Ampere.

Unsa nga unit ang atong gamiton aron sukdon ang agos sa koryente?

Ang agos sa koryente gisukod sa amperes (A)! Gipangalan kini kang Andre-Marie Ampere.

Halos bulag sa kulay ang cuttlefish, pero nakakatugma pa rin sila sa kulay ng paligid, palaisipan pa rin ito sa mga siyentista.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagpares sa kolor sa cuttlefish bisan halos buta kini sa kolor?

Halos buta sa kolor ang cuttlefish, apan makahaom gihapon sila sa kolor sa palibot, misteryo pa gihapon kini sa mga siyentista.

Why do cuttlebones wash up on the beach?

When a cuttlefish dies, its soft body rots away but the cuttlebone is left behind. Since it's full of gas and light, it floats and often washes up on the beach.

Bakit may nakikitang cuttlebone sa dalampasigan?

Kapag namatay ang cuttlefish, nabubulok ang malambot niyang katawan pero naiiwan ang cuttlebone. Dahil puno ito ng gas at magaan, lumulutang ito at madalas naiiwan sa dalampasigan.
copy.bis:
Ngano makita ang cuttlebone sa baybayon?

Kung mamatay ang cuttlefish, madunot ang humok niyang lawas apan mabilin ang cuttlebone. Tungod kay puno kini sa gas ug gaan, molutaw kini ug kasagaran maanod sa baybayon.

copy.bis:
Unsang hayop ang adunay porma-W nga kalimutaw?

The loudness of sound is measured in a special unit called the decibel (dB)!

Unsaon nato pagsukod sa kakusog sa tunog?

Ang kakusog sa tunog gisukod sa usa ka yunit nga gitawag og desibel (dB)!

Why aren't fungi considered plants?

Fungi have no chlorophyll, so unlike plants, they can't make their own food — instead they take it from dead matter around them.

Walang chlorophyll ang fungi, kaya hindi tulad ng halaman, hindi ito makakagawa ng sariling pagkain — kumukuha ito sa patay na bagay sa paligid.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili giisip nga tanom ang fungi?

Wala silay chlorophyll ang fungi, mao nga dili sama sa tanom, dili sila makahimo og kaugalingong pagkaon — mokuha kini gikan sa patay nga butang sa palibot.

copy.en:
How do deep-sea animals glow in the dark?

Bioluminescence happens when luciferin, a pigment, reacts with the enzyme luciferase — this makes light with almost no heat, unlike human-made lights.
copy.tl:
Paano nagniningning sa dilim ang mga hayop sa kailaliman ng dagat?

Nagaganap ang bioluminescence kapag ang luciferin, isang pigmento, ay nagreact sa enzyme na luciferase — gumagawa ito ng liwanag nang halos walang init, hindi tulad ng mga ilaw ng tao.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagdan-ag sa kangitngit sa mga hayop sa lawom nga dagat?

Mahitabo ang bioluminescence kung ang luciferin, usa ka pigmento, motikang sa enzyme nga luciferase — kini maghimo og suga nga halos walay kainit, dili sama sa suga nga hinimo sa tawo.

Unsang hayop ang pinakalawom molangoy?

Ang Cuvier's beaked whale mao ang pinakalawom molangoy nga hayop — miabot kini ug mga 2,992 ka metro ang giladmon!

Why does a mirror fog up when you breathe on it?

Your breath carries water vapor — you lose water every time you breathe out, not just through sweat and pee, so keep drinking water!

May singaw ng tubig na lumalabas sa iyong hininga — nawawalan ka ng tubig tuwing huminga ka, hindi lang sa pawis at ihi, kaya kailangan mong laging uminom!
copy.bis:
Ngano moganga ang salamin kon ginhawaan?

Ang imong ginhawa nagdala og singaw sa tubig — mawad-an ka og tubig matag mogawas ang imong ginhawa, dili lang sa singot ug ihi, mao nga kinahanglan kanunay moinom!

copy.en:
How can you test for dehydration?

Try this: gently pinch the skin on the back of your hand and let go. If it snaps back fast, you're fine — but if it stays tented and returns slowly, that's a sign of dehydration!
copy.tl:
Paano malalaman kung dehydrated ka?

Subukan mo ito: kurutin nang bahagya ang balat sa likod ng kamay mo at bitiwan. Kung mabilis itong bumalik, ayos ka lang — pero kung mabagal o parang naiipit, senyales ito ng dehydration!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagsuta kon dehydrated ka?

Sulayi kini: kusia og gamay ang panit sa likod sa imong kamot ug buhii. Kon paspas kini mobalik, okay ra ka — apan kon hinay o morag magtukod, timailhan kini sa dehydration!

Why do some things float while others sink?

copy.tl:
Bakit may lumulutang at may lumulubog?

Nakadepende ito sa density! Kung mas mababa ang density kaysa tubig, lumulutang. Kung mas mataas, lumulubog. Mahalaga rin ang hugis — lumulutang ang barkong bakal dahil may hangin sa loob!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang uban molutaw samtang ang uban molugdang?

Nagdepende kini sa density! Kon mas ubos ang density kaysa tubig, molutaw. Kon mas taas, molugdang. Importante sab ang porma — molutaw ang puthaw nga barko tungod kay adunay hangin sa sulod!

Ever wonder how frost appears on cold mornings?

That's deposition! It's when a gas changes straight into a solid, just like frost forming!
copy.tl:
Naisip mo ba kung paano lumalabas ang frost sa mga malamig na umaga?

Yan ang deposition! Ito yung pagbabago ng gas nang diretso tungo sa solido, tulad ng pagbuo ng frost!
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo unsaon pagporma sa frost sa bugnaw nga mga buntag?

Mao na ang deposition! Kini ang pagbag-o gikan sa gas direkta ngadto sa solido, sama sa pagporma sa frost!

What is dew?

It's the tiny drops of water on leaves and grass in the morning! They form when water vapor in the air cools down.

Ito ang maliliit na patak ng tubig sa mga dahon at damo tuwing umaga! Nabubuo ito kapag lumamig ang singaw ng tubig sa hangin.

Mao ni ang gagmayng tinulo sa tubig sa mga dahon ug sagbot sa buntag! Matawo kini kung mobugnaw ang alisngaw sa hangin.

copy.en:
Can you catch diabetes like a cold?

No — diabetes is not contagious! You can't catch it by touching someone who has it, because it's a problem with insulin inside the body, not a spreading germ.
copy.tl:
Nakakahawa ba ang diabetes tulad ng sipon?

Hindi! Hindi nakakahawa ang diabetes — hindi mo ito makukuha kahit hawakan mo ang taong may diabetes, dahil problema ito sa insulin sa katawan, hindi mikrobyong kumakalat.
copy.bis:
Makatakod ba ang diabetes sama sa sip-on?

Dili! Dili makatakod ang diabetes — dili nimo kini makuha bisan hikapon nimo ang tawo nga naay diabetes, kay problema kini sa insulin sa lawas, dili mikrobyo nga mokatag.

What causes diabetes to develop?

When the pancreas doesn't make enough insulin, blood sugar rises — and that's how diabetes can develop.

copy.bis:
Unsa ang hinungdan sa diabetes?

Kon dili igo ang insulin nga himuon sa pancreas, mosaka ang asukal sa dugo — ug mao kana ang sinugdanan sa diabetes.
